title: Session-aware SLOs for conversational sustain, recovery and graceful degradation
creator: Asha Mehta
description: Define and formalize session-aware SLOs for conversational (streaming) endpoints that cover both first-token latency and sustained throughput/quality during long sessions. This PRD captures measurable targets, error budget accounting for multi-phase sessions (initial turn vs sustain), burn-rate policies, automated fallback behaviors, and rollout gates for model and routing changes that affect streaming user experience.
context: Current SLO work focuses on token-level latency bands and p99 tail for single-shot generation. Streaming chat with persistent sessions has different failure modes: first-token latency (init latency), sustained token-per-second throughput during long responses, cumulative quality degradation across the session, and recovery after transient capacity issues. Several customers have reported degraded interactive feel during long assistant responses in multi-turn flows. This ticket bridges that gap and provides rollout-safe thresholds and gates.
goals: 1) Provide clear, testable SLO targets for session start and sustain phases. 2) Define error budget accounting that separates initial-turn failures from sustained-throughput failures. 3) Specify automated fallback routing and model degradation policies tied to SLO burn-rate. 4) Define canary and rollback gates for deployment changes that affect streaming behavior.
metrics: First-token latency: p50/p90/p99 in ms for interactive chat; Sustain throughput: mean and p95 tokens/sec for responses longer than 64 tokens; Stall rate: percentage of sessions that stop emitting tokens for >500ms during response; Availability: percentage of requests that complete (non-5xx) within configured timeout; Session-quality regressions: measured by prompt-set BLEU/ROUGE style proxies and key prompt acceptance tests.
acceptance_criteria: SLOs documented: first-token p50<120ms, p90<250ms, p99<600ms for hosted-api in us-west-2 under standard load class
Sustain throughput SLO: median tokens/sec >= 80 and p95 >= 40 for responses >64 tokens under steady-state load for dedicated capacity tier
Stall-rate SLO: <1.0% sessions with mid-response stalls >500ms for hosted tier and <0.25% for dedicated tier
Error budget definition: separate buckets for init (first-token) vs sustain; quarterly budget for init = 0.5% and sustain = 1.5% for hosted baseline
Burn-rate policy: automated throttles and model-fallback triggered when 1-hour burn-rate > 4x baseline; manual escalation when 6-hour cumulative burn-rate > 2x

Rollout gates: canary must demonstrate no >10% relative increase in stall-rate and no >5% regression in init p90 vs baseline before progressing beyond 10% traffic; automatic rollback if regression observed at canary >1.5x error budget consumption in 30 minutes
Monitoring: dashboards and composite SLO alerts created and wired to oncall with runbooks
CI: contract tests added to runtime CI that run synthetic streaming sessions and assert sustained token rates and no stalls above thresholds
Docs: PRD and runbook links published and reviewers (SRE, Runtime, Console PM) have approved
rollout_plan: Phase A: internal canary (5% traffic) for 48 hours with synthetic load and customer shadowing. Phase B: gradual ramp to 25% if canary metrics within gates for 24h. Phase C: 50% then 100% with 6-hour observation windows between ramps. At any gate fail, automatic rollback to previous model variant and routing policy. For Dedicated customers, schedule a controlled maintenance window and notify tenants; use per-tenant SLO overrides for critical customers.
monitoring: Create per-route session SLO dashboard: first-token latency histograms, sustain tokens/sec distribution, stall-rate timeseries, error-budget burn-rate chart. SLI collectors must be instrumented in the streaming runtime to tag session phase (init vs sustain) and aggregate per-customer and per-model.
alerts: Static alerts for immediate breach: session-stall-rate > 1% sustained for 5m (hosted) open P0; composite alert for error-budget burn-rate > 4x in 1h triggers automated throttle policy. Oncall runbook steps: 1) enable degraded routing (smaller model variant), 2) throttle incoming low-priority traffic, 3) open incident if rollback required.
